text:
julia: Customer on account 987654321 reported sudden 502s + intermittent 401s after migrating to an Interface VPC Endpoint for inference.private.redwoodapi.com. They cutover last night. Need quick triage — attaching repro steps below.

matt: Can you paste the minimal repro (curl) and any error lines from our ingesters? Also which region & VPC endpoint id?

julia: repro steps:
```
# from app host in prod VPC
curl -v https://inference.private.redwoodapi.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Host: inference.private.redwoodapi.com"
* Connected to 10.0.45.12 (10.0.45.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.private.redwoodapi.com
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": "upstream error: failed to fetch response" }
```
also saw STS errors in app logs: `sts:AssumeRole failed: InvalidClientTokenId` repeated right before the 502 spikes. Region eu-west-1, VPC endpoint vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h.

sarah: Two quick checks: 1) Is Private Hosted Zone resolving to VPCE private IPs (split-horizon)? 2) Are clients proxying traffic through a central egress that may rewrite SNI/Host? If SNI != cert CN you'll get TLS mismatch which some proxies surface as 502. Run `dig +short inference.private.redwoodapi.com @10.0.0.2` and `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.private.redwoodapi.com`

alex: Also remember: if the app depends on STS or other AWS public endpoints for token refresh, and the VPC egress/firewall blocks egress to sts.amazonaws.com, then token refresh will fail and app returns auth errors that cascade. Check egress allowlists/NACLs and whether STS is routed via NAT.

customer-alert-bot: Alert: Customer 987654321 increased 5xx rate 4.2x over baseline between 2026-02-12T03:12:00Z - 2026-02-12T03:18:00Z. Relevant trace ids: trace-abc-001, trace-abc-002.

matt: If STS lookups are blocked the best short-term workaround is to allow egress to `sts.amazonaws.com` (443) or ensure token refresh traffic goes via an internet NAT path that isn't hairpinned through the endpoint. Also confirm the VPCE endpoint policy isn't denying traffic to the service's canonical host. Example endpoint policy to check (quick scan):
```
{
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": "*", "Action": "*", "Resource": "*" }
  ]
}
```
(this is permissive; customers sometimes lock down by service name incorrectly and block STS/S3 access used by sidecars)

julia: did the dig + traceroute:
```
$ dig +short inference.private.redwoodapi.com
10.0.45.12

$ traceroute -n 10.0.45.12
1 10.0.1.1 0.5 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms (local)
2 10.0.254.1 2.1 ms 2.2 ms 2.0 ms (central-tgw)
3 34.210.99.8 15.7 ms 15.4 ms 15.6 ms (natgw-public-ip)
4 52.95.44.10 18.0 ms 17.9 ms 18.1 ms (redwood-api-edge)
```
this looks like hairpin: our private name resolves to VPCE IP but traffic goes via TGW -> NAT -> external edge.

sarah: That traceroute explains TLS/SNI mismatches. If traffic leaves the VPC and hits our public edge, the SNI/Host header must match the public cert. Central egress proxies sometimes rewrite SNI to a proxy hostname. Check the central proxy config — if it rewrites SNI to the proxy's cert you'll see 502 or cert mismatch errors on our side. Also check that the Private Hosted Zone is associated with the app VPC (PHZ association missing leads clients to fall back to public DNS).

alex: To confirm STS flow: can you grep the app logs for `AssumeRole` + timestamp range from the 5xx spike? If token refresh is failing you'll see repeated assume calls with 400/403 or InvalidClientTokenId. If so, the app will attempt many retries and can blow up concurrent requests (billing spike / higher egress).

julia: sample app log snippets: `2026-02-12T03:14:21Z ERROR token_refresh: sts:AssumeRole failed: InvalidClientTokenId` and shortly after `2026-02-12T03:14:32Z ERROR gateway: 502 from upstream cause=connection_reset`. Customer also admits they enabled a corporate egress firewall yesterday that blocks non-approved external domains.

matt: Sounds like two contributing issues: 1) central egress path hairpinning traffic out (so PrivateLink not actually keeping traffic internal) and 2) egress firewall blocking token endpoints. Action items:
- Ask customer to add domain allowlist for `sts.amazonaws.com` + our CA OCSP endpoints (some TLS stacks need to contact OCSP responders)
- Verify Private Hosted Zone association for the service PHZ with the app VPC (aws route53: list-vpc-association-authorizations)
- If using TGW central egress, ensure routing preserves direct-to-enis path for the vpce service or use resolver endpoints to force internal resolution

sarah: Quick check commands I usually run for this class of issues:
```
# Check PHZ association
aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id ZXXXXXXXX
# Check interface endpoint ENIs in VPC
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="*vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h*"
# Verify app host TLS to ENI ips
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.45.12:443 -servername inference.private.redwoodapi.com
```

ajax: (typo: alex) — also verify security group egress on the ENI; if SG denies return traffic you'll see asymmetric failures.

julia: I pinged the customer with these steps and they confirmed: their PHZ was associated only with the central egress VPC, not the app VPC (missed in the change). Also their egress firewall blocked sts.amazonaws.com. They will: associate PHZ with app VPC, allow sts in firewall, and test token refresh flow.

matt: Great. If they still see 502s after PHZ association, ask them to capture a tcpdump on the app host to show SYN/ACK path and whether the TLS ClientHello SNI is being rewritten by an intermediate proxy. If it is, we need to escalate to Networking to adjust proxy rules or advise them to bypass proxy for the service.

julia: Customer will cutover tomorrow morning to associate PHZ + add allowlist. I created a support ticket (INC-112233) and linked the traces. Will update here after confirmation.

matt: Thanks — cc @oncall for Post-cutover validation. If they want a fast fallback: temporary NAT route that allows app hosts to reach sts directly (bypass proxy) will unblock token refresh.

julia: marking next steps: 1) PHZ association 2) allowlist sts/OCSP 3) capture tcpdump if still failing. Will post results. :thumbsup:
